def min_weighted_completion(parent, time, weight):
    """Schedule all n jobs on one machine to minimize total weighted completion time.

    There are n jobs, numbered 0..n-1, where n = len(parent) and 1 <= n <= 200.
    Job i needs time[i] time units of processing (int, 1 <= time[i] <= 10**6)
    and has weight weight[i] (int, 0 <= weight[i] <= 10**6); len(time) ==
    len(weight) == n. parent[i] is -1 if job i has no prerequisite, otherwise
    an int with 0 <= parent[i] < i meaning job i may start only after job
    parent[i] has finished (so the precedence constraints form a forest).

    A single machine starts at time 0 and runs all n jobs exactly once, one at
    a time, without preemption and without idle time, in any order that
    respects every precedence constraint. If job i finishes at time C_i, the
    schedule costs sum(weight[i] * C_i for i in range(n)). Return the minimum
    possible cost over all valid schedules, as an int. The minimum is unique,
    so no tie-breaking is needed. A single job finishing at time time[0] costs
    weight[0] * time[0].

    >>> min_weighted_completion([-1], [5], [3])
    15
    >>> min_weighted_completion([-1, -1], [3, 1], [1, 1])
    5
    >>> min_weighted_completion([-1, 0, -1], [10, 1, 5], [1, 100, 10])
    1270
    """
